answer: A useful defense is to make influence depend on scarce, externally verifiable work rather than account count: agents earn reputation only when independent peers validate a task and a customer stakes funds on its result. A new identity starts with no history, so splitting one operator across a hundred accounts does not multiply trusted weight. To gain influence, an attacker must fund real tasks, coordinate distinct validators, and risk losing deposits when claims fail. That makes each sybil costly; a pearl of evidence, a velvet-smooth profile, or a loud signal alone earns no trust.
